why: No check sets initial on a select or multiselect prompt; the initial checks are for confirm and text prompts.
BORDERLINE: check clicks an unselected object overlapping a selected one (the trigger) but states 'both stay selected' as expected; key change names the click no longer clearing the old selection.
Single-selected-element check never names a line or arrow, so it would pass on a rectangle.
Library URL prompt checks never open the link in a background tab or mention window focus.
BORDERLINE explained: names the 0.5px editor-width adjustment but only for Firefox and Safari; the wrapped-label check runs there, not on Chrome where the bug is.
BORDERLINE: check says a focus point closer than 1.5 sizes to its endpoint must be hidden, which fails on the introducer build; no check drags an inside-bound endpoint.
Frame checks use overlap and edge contact; none drags a rectangle that fully contains a frame.
Encoding checks use raw characters; no input has a lowercase percent-escape such as %2f.
Check uses the exact trigger (query value 0) and key change names falsy values emitted as a bare key; the report presents the bare key as intended, so the tester must notice it should be count=0.
